subject: gk
question: Which of the following were NOT part of the comprehensive liberalisation reforms introduced in July 1991 ?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Demographic reforms**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The liberalisation reforms introduced in July 1991 primarily focused on economic restructuring, aimed at reducing government control and fostering market-driven growth.
 
• **Demographic reforms** were not part of these reforms, as they primarily relate to population policies, birth rates, and age distribution rather than economic liberalisation.
 
• The key components of the 1991 reforms included disinvestment of public sector enterprises, financial sector reforms, and trade and capital flow liberalisation.
 
• The reforms were designed to address the **balance of payments crisis** and stimulate economic growth by opening up the Indian economy to global markets.
 
• The government implemented measures to reduce fiscal deficits, deregulate industries, and encourage private and foreign investment in various sectors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Balance of Payments Crisis (1991):**

 
 
• India faced a severe economic crisis in 1991 due to dwindling foreign exchange reserves, rising fiscal deficits, and high inflation.
 
• The crisis necessitated immediate reforms to stabilise the economy and attract foreign investments.
 
 
 
• **Disinvestment and Public Enterprise Reforms:**
 
 
• This involved reducing government stakes in public sector undertakings (PSUs) to enhance efficiency and raise revenue.
 
• It marked a shift towards a more market-oriented approach in the management of public enterprises.
 
 
 
• **Financial Sector Reforms:**
 
 
• These reforms aimed to modernise the banking sector, reduce government control, and introduce competition among financial institutions.
 
• The establishment of the SEBI (Securities and Exchange Board of India) in 1992 strengthened capital markets.
 
 
 
• **Trade and Capital Flow Reforms:**
 
 
• Reforms included reducing trade tariffs, liberalising foreign direct investment (FDI) norms, and making the Indian rupee partially convertible on the current account.
 
• These measures aimed to integrate India with the global economy and boost exports.
 
 
 
• **Structural Adjustment Program:**
 
 
• The reforms were part of a structural adjustment program agreed upon with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) to secure financial assistance.
 
• The program emphasised macroeconomic stability, fiscal discipline, and economic liberalisation.
